notes: Round 4 (2026-11-04): four kernel-checked theorems (SubspaceCriterion, MeanCount, TransparentEncoding, BooleanNullstellensatz in research/ecdlp_weakness_lean_20261104/lean) and five exact native censuses (research/ecdlp_weakness_census_20261104). Census rows are repository measurements on small parameters; none is a pcc-verified claim (no validator key in this container).

sources.title: Exact censuses against five ECDLP hardness assumptions (Rust, 2026-11-04)
sources.citation: research/ecdlp_weakness_census_20261104: pq2_rank, pf_yield, rank_deficit, trace_pullback, ext_decomp; each crate's README and results/*.json.

nodes.label: Linear-count criterion for any finite-dimensional subspace: d_lin <= sd (Lean)
nodes.statement: If a Groebner basis of I for a degree-compatible order lies in a finite-dimensional subspace S, 1 is not in I, and I contains k polynomials whose leading monomials are k distinct variables, then k <= dim(S intersect {totalDegree <= 1}). For S = the span of the Macaulay rows of degree <= d: if that dimension is < k, no Groebner basis lies in the degree-d row space, so the Caminata-Gorla solving degree exceeds d.
nodes.scope: Generalises THM-SD-DEGREE2-CRITERION from span(F) to any subspace; the census quantity d_lin (least d with low_d >= k) is a lower bound on sd.

nodes.label: Unique F_2-solution puts every X_i - z_i in the ideal (Lean)
nodes.statement: Over F_2, with the field equations adjoined to a finite family F: a polynomial vanishing on all of F_2^N lies in the field-equation ideal; and if z is the only common zero of F, then X_i - z_i lies in the ideal of F and the field equations for every i.
nodes.scope: The |Z| = 1 case of the bridge k = N - affdim(Z) used by the pq2_rank census. The general-Z case (affine span) is not formalised.

nodes.label: Mean ordered representation count is exactly |F|^m / |G| (Lean)
nodes.statement: In a finite additive group G with factor base F and arity m, the ordered representation counts N(R) sum to |F|^m over all targets R, so their mean is |F|^m / |G|.
nodes.scope: The counting half of HEUR-DECOMPOSITION-PROBABILITY; the distribution shape remains the heuristic part.

nodes.label: 'Every algorithm needs Omega(sqrt r) group operations for DLP in a prime-order group'
nodes.statement: Overbroad reading of Shoup's bound: any discrete-logarithm algorithm in a group of prime order r performs Omega(sqrt r) group operations.
nodes.scope: False as stated: the bound is for generic algorithms under random encodings. With a transparent encoding the logarithm is read off with no group operation.

nodes.label: Z/r with the identity encoding: the logarithm is the encoding (Lean)
nodes.statement: In ZMod r with generator 1, h.val * 1 = h; for any cyclic group with an encoding enc(x * g) = x, the output enc(h) is a correct logarithm, computed with zero group operations.
nodes.scope: Shows the bound is relative to the encoding model; it does not weaken Shoup's theorem on its own terms.

nodes.label: Prime-field m = 2 yield census: Poisson(mu/2) zero class, 1.45x dispersion for negation-closed bases
nodes.statement: On 18 prime-order curves with p from 2003 to 80021 and factor bases with B^2/r in {0.5, 1, 2}: for unordered pair counts U(R), P(U >= 1) matches 1 - exp(-mean U) within about 1% on average for small-x, random and random negation-closed bases; var(U)/mean(U) is about 1.45 for both negation-closed bases and 0.97-0.99 for the random base not closed under negation. The ordered count N = 2U + diagonal, so the ordered prediction 1 - exp(-B^2/r) overstates the decomposable fraction by the pairing factor (ratio 0.56-0.76).
nodes.scope: Exact enumeration of every target; small p. Overdispersion tracks negation-closure of the base, not the small-x shape.

nodes.label: Right-kernel relation matrices: Delta = 10 does not give full rank (10 curves, 5 samples)
nodes.statement: Random-point relations a G = P1 + P2 over small-x factor bases (B ~ sqrt r) on 10 prime-order curves, p from 1009 to 16001: with negation pairs merged into B/2 unknowns, Delta = 10 surplus relations gave full rank in all 5 samples on 2 of 10 curves; the maximal deficit at Delta = 10 was 1-3 and at Delta = 40 up to 2. Free relations P1 + P2 = P3 among factor-base points span 3 to 15 of the B/2 unknowns.
nodes.scope: Single-target left-kernel use is unaffected (THM-LEFT-KERNEL-RELATIONS); this measures the multi-target / right-kernel regime where HEUR-RELATION-RANK is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Trace images of one-dimensional subspace factor bases are at least 0.32 of E(F_p)
nodes.statement: For 10 prime-order curves with p from 103 to 2003 base-changed to F_{p^2}, over all p + 1 one-dimensional F_p-subspaces V: min_V |Tr(F'_V)| / #E(F_p) is 0.32-0.39, attained at V = F_p i in every case; the median is 0.60-0.67 and V = F_p gives all of E(F_p).
nodes.scope: Dimension-1 subspaces of F_{p^2} only; higher degree extensions and higher-dimensional V not covered.

nodes.label: n-fold decomposition over F_{q^n}: 0.70-0.99 of 1/n! at n = 2, 3; premise fails for subfield curves
nodes.statement: For curves with coefficients in F_{q^n} and factor base x in F_q: the decomposable fraction is 0.350-0.413 at n = 2 (q = 101, 211, 401), 0.101-0.165 at n = 3 (q = 23, 41, 61), i.e. 0.70-0.99 of 1/n!, with |F| about q. For curves defined over F_q the factor base is E(F_q) (n odd) or lies in a small subgroup, and the fraction is 0.0003-0.002 at n = 3.
nodes.scope: Small q; n = 4 rows have factor bases of 10-18 points and scatter widely.

nodes.label: m = 2 descended S3: iterated degree-3 closure misses the linear consequences for n = 15 and 17-44
nodes.statement: Weil-descended third summation polynomial systems over F_{2^n} (ordinary binary curves, random subspace factor base of dimension ceil(n/2), field equations included), 119 instances for n = 8 to 47. The degree-d closure of the generators (every multiple within degree d of each new polynomial, until the rank is stable) reaches all k = N - affdim(Z) linear consequences at d = 3 for every n <= 14 and n = 16, and reaches only 1 of them at n = 15 and on all 84 instances with 17 <= n <= 44. On 24 fresh instances at n = 17 to 24 the degree-4 closure reaches k. The one-shot Macaulay matrix reaches 1 linear polynomial at degree 2 on every instance.
nodes.scope: Finite range n <= 47; lower bounds on F4's maximal step degree under the containment of F4's output in the degree-D closure, which is not formalised; the one-shot bound d_lin <= sd is THM-SD-SUBSPACE-CRITERION. Cannot refute an asymptotic o(1) statement.

edges.statement: A per-instance lower bound d_lin on the solving degree, computable by linear algebra at any n.
For instances with a unique solution the linear-consequence count k = N is kernel-checked.
The mean is a theorem; only the distribution shape is heuristic.
Zero group operations suffice with a transparent encoding.
The bound is relative to random encodings; representation-specific algorithms are outside it.
'Optimal by Shoup' is optimality among generic algorithms only.
The transparent-encoding countermodel is kernel-checked; the random-injective-encoding formalisation remains open.
Zero class matches Poisson once the unordered convention is used; the variance is 1.45x Poisson for negation-closed bases.
Delta = 10 left a rank deficit in at least one of 5 samples on 8 of 10 small curves.
Rank deficit as a function of surplus in the right-kernel regime.
No one-dimensional subspace of F_{p^2} gives a small trace image on the tested curves.
0.70-0.99 of 1/n! at n = 2, 3 for curves with F_{q^n} coefficients; the premise fails for subfield curves.

The solver degree exceeds the first fall degree 2 on the 111 instances with n <= 44, and the Kousidis-Wiemers value 3 is not reached for 17 <= n <= 44; exactly 4 on 24 fresh instances at n = 17 to 24.
Runs the rank census this gap asked for, with the iterated closure as the F4 proxy.
The criterion turns each low_d < k count into a degree lower bound.
